candidate.answerReason: The price after March is 120% of its starting value. Returning to the starting value requires a decrease of 20/120 = 1/6, or 16⅔%, which rounds to 17%.

methods.label: Start with 100 price units
methods.explanation:
Each percentage change acts on the current price. Scaling all prices by the same positive factor changes none of these percentages, so take the starting price to be \(100\) units.

The prices after January, February, and March are respectively
\[
100(1.20)=120,\qquad
120(0.80)=96,\qquad
96(1.25)=120.
\]
April must therefore reduce the price from \(120\) back to \(100\). The decrease is \(20\) units, measured against April's starting price of \(120\), so
\[
x=\frac{20}{120}\cdot100
=\frac{50}{3}=16.666\ldots.
\]
To the nearest integer, \(\boxed{x=17}\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Successive percentage calculations and rounding are elementary arithmetic within AMC 12 scope.
